name: ISO 45001 (Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems)
description: Requirements for an occupational health and safety management system, on the Annex SL structure (clauses 4 to 10). It shares its architecture with ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 27001:2022, so a single management-review, internal-audit and corrective-action process can serve all three. Its distinguishing requirements against COR are clause 5.4 (consultation and participation of workers, including non-managerial workers) and clause 8.1.4 (procurement, contractors and outsourcing) — both are where an auditor probes whether the system is real.
scope: Any organization seeking to manage occupational health and safety risks systematically
changes_summary: ISO 45001:2018 is the current edition and the one certificates are held against. A revision is under way in ISO/TC 283 and has reached Draft International Standard stage: the DIS ballot opened 17 June 2026 and closed 9 August 2026. No publication or transition date is recorded here because none has been set by ISO; the working drafts emphasise work-related well-being, workforce diversity and hazard identification for modern ways of working, but a draft is not a standard and nothing in this file should be changed until the revision is published.

families.name: Clause 4 — Context of the Organization
families.description: Scope of the OH&S management system and the workers it covers.

controls.name: Needs and Expectations of Workers and Other Interested Parties
controls.description: Workers, unions, regulators, clients and other interested parties are identified along with their relevant requirements.

controls.name: Scope of the OH&S Management System
controls.description: The boundaries of the system are documented and include all activities, workers and workplaces under the organization's control or influence.

families.name: Clause 5 — Leadership and Worker Participation
families.description: The clause that separates ISO 45001 from a paper safety programme.

controls.name: Leadership and Commitment
controls.description: Top management takes overall responsibility for preventing work-related injury and ill health, provides safe workplaces, and protects workers from reprisal when reporting.

controls.name: OH&S Policy
controls.description: A policy commits to safe and healthy working conditions, hazard elimination, worker consultation and legal compliance, and is communicated to workers.

controls.name: Organizational Roles, Responsibilities and Authorities
controls.description: Responsibility and authority for the OH&S system are assigned at all levels, communicated and maintained as documented information.

controls.name: Consultation and Participation of Workers
controls.description: Non-managerial workers are consulted and participate in hazard identification, incident investigation and OH&S planning, with barriers to participation identified and removed.

families.name: Clause 6 — Planning
families.description: Hazard identification, legal requirements and OH&S objectives.

controls.name: Hazard Identification and Assessment of Risks
controls.description: Hazards are identified proactively and on an ongoing basis, accounting for routine and non-routine activities, emergencies, human factors and changes; risks are assessed with a documented methodology.

controls.name: Determination of Legal and Other Requirements
controls.description: Applicable legal requirements are identified, kept current, and their implications for the organization are communicated to workers.

controls.name: Planning Action (Hierarchy of Controls)
controls.description: Actions to address hazards and risks apply the hierarchy of controls — eliminate, substitute, engineer, administrate, then PPE — with the choice justified.

controls.name: OH&S Objectives and Planning to Achieve Them
controls.description: Measurable OH&S objectives are set, resourced, assigned and monitored, and are consistent with the policy.

families.name: Clause 7 — Support
families.description: Competence, awareness, communication and documented information.

controls.name: Competence
controls.description: Workers are competent to identify hazards and perform their work safely, with competence based on training, education or experience and retained as evidence.

controls.name: Awareness
controls.description: Workers are aware of the OH&S policy, the hazards relevant to them, incidents and outcomes, and their right to remove themselves from imminent danger.

controls.name: Documented Information
controls.description: OH&S documented information is controlled, current, available where needed, and retained for the statutory period.

families.name: Clause 8 — Operation
families.description: Operational control, management of change, contractors and emergency preparedness.

controls.name: Eliminating Hazards and Reducing OH&S Risks
controls.description: Operational controls are established and maintained to eliminate hazards or reduce risk, applied per the hierarchy of controls.

controls.name: Management of Change
controls.description: Changes to processes, equipment, personnel or legal requirements are assessed for OH&S consequence before implementation.

controls.name: Procurement, Contractors and Outsourcing
controls.description: Procurement controls ensure conformity; contractor OH&S criteria are applied and coordinated, and outsourced functions remain controlled.

controls.name: Emergency Preparedness and Response
controls.description: Emergency situations are identified and planned for, response is tested periodically, and plans are communicated to workers and relevant contractors and visitors.

families.name: Clause 9 — Performance Evaluation
families.description: Monitoring, compliance evaluation, internal audit and management review.

controls.name: Evaluation of Compliance with Legal Requirements
controls.description: Compliance with applicable legal and other requirements is evaluated at a defined frequency, with results and actions retained.

controls.name: Internal Audit
controls.description: Internal audits assess conformity of the OH&S system on a planned programme, conducted objectively and reported to management and workers.

controls.name: Management Review
controls.description: Top management reviews the OH&S system at planned intervals against defined inputs including incident trends, participation and compliance status.

families.name: Clause 10 — Improvement
families.description: Incident investigation, corrective action and continual improvement.

controls.name: Incident, Nonconformity and Corrective Action
controls.description: Incidents and nonconformities are reported, investigated for root cause including system causes, corrective action taken, and effectiveness reviewed.

controls.name: Continual Improvement
controls.description: OH&S performance is continually improved, promoting a positive safety culture and worker participation in improvement actions.
